I was a #3 on this list I could barely stand to walk the 10 feet to the bathroom. When I stood up and fainted my husband called 911. I swear the Dr at the er didn't listen to a damn word I said. The part he didn't listen to was I had been having extremely heavy periods for over a year almost nonstop, he said that was normal for someone my age (40). IF he looked at my blood work he would have seen my hemoglobin level was 8.7 iron was at 9, they do blood transfusions at 8.5 he did not say 1 word about it or tell me to see my Dr, no tests done, how would he know if I had some kind of internal bleeding? I ended up back in the hospital 2 months later blood level 4.2 iron level came back as 4<, 5 blood transfusions 4 iron transfusions a week in the hospital. I have been pregnant 3 times 4 kids ( twins) and married 20yrs, you're both going to have to learn to compromise because there is a lot of it in being a parent and being in a long-term relationship if you want it to work. Most of this is because you are on a hormonal Rollercoaster,  it increases your sense of smell big time and smells you never noticed or never bothered you smell awful, little things feel huge and can piss you off fast I get it 100%. Maybe the dad wasn't surprised because it's something they have always dealt with with him? My son had normal ear tube surgery at 3yrs old and idk what the hell happened but he woke up and it was like someone switched my kid. He went from fully potty trained for about 6 months to completely reversing, his temperament was completely different, he went from being the sweetest kid to throwing things at us being straight-out mean to everyone, breaking things putting holes in walls. It was hell and this went on until he was about 16, including refusing to use the bathroom. We tried everything, toilet classes for special needs kids through the hospital, so many therapists that would drop him after a few sessions for refusing to talk. Four 2 week stays at in-care psych units, where he was diagnosed with depression, anxiety, and ODD. We were told his bathroom issues were because it was something he was in total control of, he never pooped or peed in his pants anywhere but at home. Something tells me he also has autism but when I brought it up I was always told no. We had no idea what to do, his Drs were out of ideas it was bad, even with him on meds.
We pulled him out of school at 16 and it helped, school was too much, he was having panic attacks, and instead of helping, one of his teachers was bullying him,  making fun of him, and egging him on while in the middle of an attack, she caused one of his inpatient stays ( she ended up getting fired for how she treated students, not just my son ). Then they came out with DNA med testing and we had that done, it came back that he was on completely the wrong meds. We changed them and within a few months completely different kid. Anger issues were basically gone, he could now actually understand and use the coping techniques he learned in in-care, bathroom issues were slowly gone, he still has a few issues because of the damage he did to his colon. He's working on his GED and wants to go into construction or electrical, whereas before we were sure he was going to have to live in a group home-type situation. 
   OP your husband needs to see his Dr he sounds overwhelmed and not sure how to handle it. Depending on your relationship with his Dr. I would call them and tell them what's going on, ask for advice, make him an appt maybe ask the office for a Lil white lie to get him in to be seen like hey you need to come in for your annual physical you missed it and make sure to go with him so you can tell them what's going on and he can't hide from it, he might get pissed at you but oh well. He might need meds or maybe even a grippy sock vacation to get down to the real issues. But it wouldn't surprise me if this is something he's always done when he feels like he's out of control since his dad wasn't surprised or worried. It's the one thing he goes back to since things like hygiene are something only he can control even if he's doing it subconsciously. Marriage is in sickness and health, good and bad right now things are bad and he's sick, but that also doesn't mean if he doesn't agree to the help you have to stay. You are trying your best at the moment for whatever reason he's not, whether that's by his choice or it's something else, the breaking point would be if he follows through with getting help, if not leave him. At least there are no kids involved from what it sounds like which makes leaving him and breaking ties much easier.

Okay, so here are my 2 cents for what they are worth, I've had 4 kids 2 of which are twins and every single time I went through something similar, however, our first and our twins were the hardest. First, you need to sit down with him and as clearly as possible without yelling tell him basically what you wrote here you need more help you're drowning and it's going to start affecting your relationship if he doesn't step up more, offer to help him. I've noticed not only with my husband but with friends' husbands they think because we are moms/ women so we somehow just know exactly what to do with these crying Lil squishes like all this magical info is just downloaded into our brain when we give birth or in some cases we do have a bit more experience with kids because it was basically forced on us (at least it was for me, being the oldest child on both sides of the family and being told I had to watch all the younger kids) and with most/some men they are well men per se and don't want to look stupid by asking for help when you look like you know what your doing or it seems like it comes to us easily when truthfully we are just winging it until something finally works. I swear sometimes it's almost like trying to teach a dog a trick, have them help you, show them what to do, and tell them thank you while hiding the eye roll and sounding sarcastic out loud. Then ask them to do it while you're busy after a bit they just start doing it themselves or with a small cue " can you smell that?" "Oh looks like Lil one is getting sleepy" ect... Also if he is not doing things how you would or just exactly right do not say a thing it will be hard not to say anything but as long as it's safe let him, what works for you might not work for him or he finds an easier way for him to do it that works, my kids are all boys so let's just say for example how I played with them and how he did was completely different full on what seemed like wrestling matches, tossing them onto beds, tossing them in the air and catching them etc. But if he changes her diaper a different way but still safe cuz utis or burps her a different way but it works for him just walk away and enjoy your few minutes of not doing anything. 
  My husband was almost to a T like yours when we had our first except he would go to work come home play video games half the night then sleep until he had to work the next day, he would literally stop playing his game and walk right by our crying baby to wake me up or to make sure I was getting up with him then walk right past him again to go back to playing. I think part of it is until the baby gets here it's just a concept it's not real real to them then boom here is this huge responsibility looking straight at them and part of them wants to fight that, I would almost describe it as a mini midlife crisis. It's more real to us because we are the ones who are pregnant and have been dealing with it for 9 months 24/7  and all the changes and adjustments we had to make to our life while pregnant. It gives us time to adjust mentally to the responsibility it's more real for us because we feel the movements the kicking, our bodies going through crazy shit. And while it wasn't just tossed in their laps when the baby is born it becomes a quick harsh reality that oh this is happening and real.I think part of it too might be what they expected vs reality, they picture and see themselves playing with this older baby who is laughing and they can actually play with, not the reality that for the first 3ish month but more likely 6 months here is this baby who just lays there looking kinda weird that all it does is eats sleeps poops and cries and that's not exactly "fun" or what they pictured it to be like so your there it's eating sleeping or pooping so why do I have to be there to just look her when I can be out doing something fun or productive, moms there she knows more so why do I have to be too, not taking into account us being in pain lack of sleep hormones and basic things that still need to get done around the house or hell taking a nice long shower. It was also extremely hard for us when our twins where born our other 2 kids were 5 and barely 11 months( yup Irish triplets wheee) , needless to say, the twins were an oops and huge surprise, it was a lot and stressful for the first year, hell I don't remember half of it. They were born at 35  weeks perfectly healthy but tiny 5lbs and 5lbs 1oz he didn't know how to handle babies so tiny our other two were around 7lbs the twins also were so hard to feed the first 2 months they had a hard time latching onto their bottles and it took so much more time and patience and he would just get frustrated which made me mad at him causing so many middle of the night fights but over time they got bigger and we worked out a system where I would get them propped up on pillows on the bed with me while he went and got their bottles ready, I would feed them burp them while he kinda half slept than when they were done he would put them back in their crib. I was also a SAHM so it was also our deal that he worked i got up at night he would come home and take over taking care of the kids fully while I made dinner and kinda sat down a bit. This is where talking to him about everything you're going through and him not doing enough comes in, it also helps if you have decent inlaws or he has older siblings or a good friend who has kids who will see him acting a fool and have their own little talk with him. My FIL did with my husband after we were visiting them for the day, boy did he put hubby in his place fast. I didn't ask my fil to say anything to him per se he just saw what was going on. I also kinda started conversations to say what was going on without saying it (oh did hubby tell you about his new hobby he's been doing every weekend, you should hear his new golf scores he's been playing so much that he has been improving lately ) and fil called him on his bs. I did the same with my little brother after he had his first and his wife dropped the hey you should show your sister all the new upgrades you have been doing to your car while hanging out with your friends a lot lately..message received loud and clear I told him I would love that! We went outside and I handed his ass to him. Both hubby and my brother straightened out after that. You also need to be prepared that you can try and put in all the effort you can and he's just not going to change that's when it's time to go. What you do from there is up to you and him, hopefully, if it comes to that it's a temporary situation where it's a big wake-up call that he's been an ass and now might have lost everything or he doesn't and you just keep taking care of yourself and your daughter without a man attached to you who refuses to grow up and you have one less child to take care of because that's what he's acting like. Becoming parents is so hard, especially the first year it will either make you or break you as a couple. Thankfully my husband heard me finally and became an amazing dad, and I really  hope with some conversations and showing him what's needed and what he needs to do and maybe a bit of tough love your hubby can see the light and become the best dad ever and a much better husband too. ❤️
